title: the-owner-is-a-database-and-every-link-is-a-tuple
intention: Every durable leaf has the address <owner>.<table>.<leaf>, the owner segment IS a Postgres database of that owner's own, every link is a tuple of two addresses readable from both ends, and the fixed lists (embeddings, blobs, records) are positional, void-and-reuse, never deleted.
why: Akien's vision, recorded whole 2026-09-06 at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-the-vision-that-guides-every-decision.md: a household and a lab with several principals and one Igor serving all of them, so 'the problem of who owns what takes on a new dimension'. Ruled the same day: 'the per owner database is a thing we do before things become even more complicated.' Measured the same day: cairn_links holds 0 rows, so the link tuple has no installed base to retrofit; every day after the cast it grows one.
traces_to: Law 6 (ownership in the address, and the owner's gate is now a database boundary, which is physics per Law 4); Law 1 (provenance derived from the link structure, never re-derived); telos 3 (share those tools with others: the vision's household and lab need several principals). Ruling 2026-09-06-the-per-owner-database-comes-before-more-complexity. Intention I-universal-addressing-and-bidirectional-links.md; use case I-the-vision-that-guides-every-decision.md.

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate — cairn/devices/db_domain/proofs/test_per_owner_addressing.py (new): the seven falsifier teeth as seven functions against `cairn_test_*` databases created and dropped by the proof; plus test_db_domain.py, test_sole_path.py and cairn/devices/librarian/proofs/ staying green. Feeds back naming the tooth that broke. Durability: committed in cairn; sealed by the tester with source_fingerprint over db_domain.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when, on this box: (1) `psql -l` lists cairn_librarian, cairn_codemother, cairn_inference_domain and cairn_bus, and the migrated row counts equal the source counts measured 2026-09-06 (cairn_nodes 10,538; cairn_embeddings 11,230; librarian_nodes 148; codemother_root_nodes 47); (2) address.parse/render round-trips every address in a fixture set including file addresses with env vars; (3) a write to a librarian table through connect('codemother') is refused, loudly; (4) a link written from owner A to owner B appears in both link tables, and after A voids its row, links_to(B's address) still names A's row from B's side, so nothing orphans; (5) void then allocate on an embeddings list reuses the voided row id; (6) grep finds no `dbname=` and no DB_NAME outside store.py; test_db_domain.py, test_sole_path.py and the librarian's tree proofs stay green after migration. WRONG INTENT if a consumer turns out to need a cross-owner SQL join (the design says links are addresses the store resolves, never joins), or if one box for one person needs more than one Postgres role to run.

constraints: No cross-database SQL join, ever: a link is two addresses the store resolves.
db_domain stays the sole connection path (test_sole_path.py is the tooth).
No read gate (clearance) invented here; the ticket lands the one seam it will sit on and names it.
Write-gate semantics unchanged: non-owner refused, unregistered refused, where-less refused.

Ownership model confirmed by Akien ('exactly yes'): an employer delegates access to an employee. Each principal (Akien, CC, an Igor, the librarian, each device) holds its own creds; per-owner database is what a credential is for.

Until the hardening step before sharing, the librarian is allowed access to everything ('for now, the librarian is just allowed access to everything'). The migration and store.read(address) may rely on that; nothing may assume the read gate is closed.

The old `cairn` database IS dropped in this voyage, after the migration's count assertions pass: ticket 201a37bf1613 sweeps its 9,075 scratch tables out first, so nothing but the twelve live tables remains to copy (amended 2026-09-06 by CC under the delegated ordering; the earlier line assigned the drop to the scratch ticket).
how: db_domain grows the address, the per-owner database and the link tuple in one voyage; the librarian, bus, inference_domain and codemother callers move onto them; a migration carries the live rows across and leaves the old `cairn` database read-only. (1) ADDRESS: db_domain/address.py parses and renders `<owner>.<table>.<leaf>`; file-side addresses are `file:<path>` with env vars allowed. (2) PER-OWNER DATABASE: store.connect(owner) reaches Postgres database `cairn_<owner>`, created on first touch the way ensure_database creates `cairn` today; DB_NAME retires; the owner registry (`cairn_owned`, CHECK owner <> '') lives inside each owner's database and records that owner's tables, so a write to owner B's table through connect(A) is refused by the database boundary before the registry ever looks. Reads of another owner's address go through store.read(address), which opens that owner's database; this is the seam a clearance (read gate) lands on later, and it is the only cross-owner route (db_domain is the ruled exception to no-cross-device-imports). (3) LINK TUPLE: each owner's database carries `links` with local, remote, kind, weight, traversals, created, unique(local, remote), indexed on remote; a link between two owners is written in both owners' tables, each side writing its own half, so Law 6 holds and reverse traversal (links_to(address)) is a local read on either side. (4) LISTS: embeddings, blobs and records carry integer row ids with a `voided` flag; void(address) flips it and returns the reverse links; allocate(table) reuses the lowest voided row. (5) MIGRATION: db_domain/migrate_to_per_owner.py, shaped like the librarian's migrate_to_three_tables.py, copies the twelve registered system tables to their owners' databases (cairn_nodes/embeddings/links/threads and librarian_nodes to cairn_librarian; codemother_root_nodes to cairn_codemother; inference_calls to cairn_inference_domain; bus_traffic and its delivery table to cairn_bus), asserts the row counts, and leaves the 9,075 scratch tables in the old database for the scratch-tables ticket to drop.
